newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU merger panel advises banning Cablevision deal.
newsitem.headline: EU merger panel advises banning Cablevision deal.

text.p: A European Union merger panel has advised the European Commission to ban the Spanish Cablevision TV deal, EU sources said on Monday.
The advisory committee, which consists of national competition policy officials, met in Brussels to discuss the case.
"The discussion at the committee showed that everybody except Spain was of the opinion that the proposal on the table is unacceptable," one source said.
The Commission usually follows the view of the committee.
The deadline for a Commission decision on whether to clear the venture is on November 26.

The joint venture was set up by Telefonica and Sogecable SA, a unit of Promotora de Informaciones SA and France's Canal Plus, in July 1995 to operate and distribute pay television and multimedia in Spain via cable TV networks.
When it began a full probe into the case in July, the Commission expressed strong doubts about it because Telefonica still has a monopoly on the local telecommunications market.
EU sources said earlier that Telefonica was set to pull out of the venture due to Commission opposition.
The partly state-owned Spanish telecoms operator preferred to drop out now rather than face the expected ruling against the venture, they said.
